caption:
Why did the most powerful man alive keep a diary nobody was meant to read?

Marcus Aurelius left little notes on where he was writing. The end of Book 1 says "Among the Quadi at the Granua", a frontier war on the Danube. Book 2 ends "This in Carnuntum", an army base. He was writing to himself in camp, between campaigns, and it shows: every page talks to "thee".

No audience means no performance. That's why a 1,800-year-old notebook still reads like someone who gets it.

Send this to the friend who drafts texts in their notes app. 📓

Diary or drafts?

— Moodius

#marcusaurelius #meditations #stoicism #history #journaling

caption:
Don't send that text yet…

Epictetus had a two-word rule, as a Roman writer remembered it: bear and forbear. Put up with it, and hold back. Seneca, writing about anger, praised the general Fabius for knowing how to delay, the one skill angry people don't have.

So: save it as a draft. Read it at breakfast. Send the version you'd happily read out loud with your gran in the room.

Send this to the friend whose drafts folder is a crime scene. 🫣

Send or sleep?

— Moodius

#stoicism #epictetus #seneca #anger #selfcontrol
